headline: Innoviz Technologies to cut 20% of workforce
summary: Israeli LiDAR developer Innoviz Technologies is laying off 80 employees, representing roughly 20 percent of its workforce, following a one-year vehicle launch delay by a major automotive client. The reduction marks the company's third consecutive year of job cuts as it faces continuous cash burn and a sharp decline in market valuation. To offset delayed automotive revenues, Innoviz is relying on recent capital raises and expanding into the defense sector.

headline: Centre allows govt officers to retain official laptops after 4 years
summary: India's Finance Ministry has updated device procurement rules, allowing central government officers to retain official laptops and tablets after four years of use, provided stored data is erased. The revised policy also increases the device purchase budget up to Rs 1.8 lakh, prioritizing equipment with over 40 per cent domestic content. Full eligibility is extended to officers in Pay Level 12 and above, while lower pay levels receive capped coverage based on departmental needs.

headline: iD Fresh Food opens entrepreneurial path for employees with paid sabbaticals
summary: iD Fresh Food has launched a program offering mentorship, network access, and partially paid sabbaticals to employees looking to start their own businesses. The policy provides a financial and professional safety net by allowing staff to return to the company if their ventures prove unsuccessful. CEO Musthafa PC aims to actively support employee entrepreneurial ambitions rather than viewing their departure strictly as a retention loss.

headline: Nikunj Singh takes charge as head of HR at Edunet Foundation
summary: Nikunj Singh has been appointed as Human Resources Director at Edunet Foundation, assuming the role in November 2026. Bringing over two decades of HR leadership experience, Singh will lead the organization's HR department and align people strategies with organizational growth. He previously held HR and talent acquisition leadership roles at SkillLabs, Chandigarh University, and Teleperformance.

headline: IBM ends US visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
summary: IBM has ceased U.S. visa and green card sponsorships for most roles within its consulting division due to evolving talent availability and client demands. Affected U.S.-based employees have been given the option to transition to roles outside the country or leave the firm by the end of 2026. The move comes amid heightened U.S. regulatory scrutiny and rising costs associated with employment-based foreign worker programs.

headline: Cognizant introduces AI-based role framework for employees
summary: IT services firm Cognizant has launched an AI Builder Role Catalogue to redefine job roles across India and North America based on how artificial intelligence is altering workplace responsibilities. The framework categorizes positions into current, evolving, and future roles to align its workforce with AI adoption, while leaving existing compensation and reporting structures unchanged.

headline: Case-in-Point: The mental health accommodation limit
summary: UrbanCare Hospitals is facing a complex operational dilemma after a senior cardiologist requested reduced shifts due to medically documented severe burnout and anxiety. With the cardiology department already suffering from long-term staffing shortages, leadership must balance accommodating employee mental health against maintaining patient safety and avoiding additional strain on remaining staff. The hospital's CHRO is evaluating potential solutions, including a phased workload adjustment alongside urgent efforts to address recruitment needs.

headline: herSTORY: Shaili Tyagi, CHRO, Somany Impresa Group
summary: Shaili Tyagi, Chief Human Resources Officer at Somany Impresa Group, built a prominent HR career across multinationals and family-run businesses after unexpectedly transitioning from botany. Throughout her professional journey, she has advocated for continuous learning, actionable gender inclusion, and balancing business objectives with empathetic employee management during organizational changes.

headline: Logitech turns gaming into a workplace benefit with paid-time-off policy
summary: Logitech has introduced a new global benefit offering its 7,000 employees a paid day off to play video games, timed around the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. The initiative is rooted in company research linking gaming skills—such as focus, composure, and strategic decision-making—to improved workplace performance. The policy reflects a growing trend of corporate well-being strategies that leverage recreational activities to enhance long-term productivity and innovation.

headline: Tasmac nandates three-year job rotation to tackle staffing gaps
summary: The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) has announced a mandatory three-year job rotation policy for retail employees starting November 2026 to optimize workforce deployment across its 38 districts. Under the new policy, outlets will be categorized into three tiers based on daily sales to establish standardized staffing requirements. Additionally, Tasmac will initiate a one-time statewide manpower rationalization by late 2026 and institutionalize annual transfer counseling starting in 2028.

headline: Child labour compliance failure costs Walmart nearly $8 million
summary: Walmart has agreed to pay nearly $8 million to settle extensive child labor law violations in Pennsylvania following a state investigation into underage worker injuries and schedule non-compliance. The settlement requires the retail giant to pay administrative penalties and implement enhanced compliance training and safeguards for young employees. In response, Walmart stated that it maintains labor compliance processes and will continue to regularly review and refine its systems.

headline: Franklin Templeton picks Saurabh Arora to head HR in India
summary: Global investment management firm Franklin Templeton has appointed Saurabh Arora as its new Head of Human Resources for India, based in Mumbai. Arora brings extensive financial sector experience, having previously held senior HR roles at Waterfield Advisors, Russell Investments, and Morgan Stanley. His appointment aims to strengthen the company's talent strategy and India operations amid rising competition in the industry.

headline: Employee strikes and protests intensify across regions
summary: A wave of employee strikes and protests is intensifying across India, South Korea, and Spain as workers push for fair pay, job security, and broader socio-economic reforms. The labor actions threaten significant disruptions to essential public services, including municipal sanitation, healthcare, transit networks, and general commercial operations. This global surge in collective action underscores rising worker expectations and mounting pressure on organizations to resolve long-standing workplace grievances.

headline: Burson announces senior leadership changes across APAC & the US
summary: Global communications agency Burson has appointed Yuliani Setiadi as APAC head of Influence and Social and Davitha Tiller as US chair for the practice. Joining from Edelman and Havas respectively, the two leaders complete Burson's regional leadership structure under Global Chief Influence and Social Officer Matt Buchanan. The strategic hires are aimed at expanding the agency's social and influencer marketing capabilities across key global markets.

headline: HDFC SKY highlights investing features through new campaign films
summary: HDFC SKY, the discount broking platform of HDFC Securities, has launched eight new films as part of its 'Make Money Matter' marketing campaign. The series uses relatable everyday scenarios to showcase key platform features, such as US stock SIPs, fractional investing, and portfolio management tools. The campaign aims to demystify complex financial products and will be distributed across both digital channels and television.

The campaign highlights the developer's design focus on cross-ventilation, natural light, and open green spaces across its residential and commercial projects. Running through 2026 across multiple media platforms, the multi-year initiative supports ESBEE as it expands its footprint with seven million square feet in active development and upcoming pipelines.

headline: Akhilendra Kumar appointed CEO of Unacademy
summary: Edtech company Unacademy has appointed former Chief Business Officer Akhilendra Kumar as its new Chief Executive Officer, while co-founder Gaurav Munjal transitions to the role of executive chairman. Munjal will remain actively involved in daily operations and help prepare for the proposed IPO of parent firm upGrad. Kumar, who joined Unacademy in 2022 after working at OYO, takes the helm shortly after upGrad completed its $200 million acquisition of Unacademy.

headline: Mia wants jewellery out of the locker and into everyday life this festive season
summary: Mia by Tanishq is targeting younger consumers this festive season by positioning lightweight, affordable jewellery for everyday self-expression rather than traditional locker storage. To differentiate in a cluttered market, the brand has launched its 'Lightscapes' collection priced mostly under Rs 50,000, supported by self-purchase advertising campaigns and experiential marketing.

Additionally, Bosch is advancing its electric vehicle component strategy through a proposed joint venture.

headline:
Govt
extends medical devices PLI to FY36, relaxes rules to spur investment
summary: The Indian government has extended its Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for domestic medical device manufacturing through FY36, making available an outlay of approximately ₹2,700 crore. The overhauled PLI-MD 2.0 framework removes rigid minimum sales targets and lowers investment thresholds to ease entry barriers for domestic manufacturers. The initiative aims to deepen local supply chain integration, boost high-end diagnostic equipment manufacturing, and reduce India's heavy reliance on imported MedTech.
